STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal of fried/roasted chicken pieces (bone-in, skin partly crisp), sliced cucumber, and boiled cauliflower florets. Looks like a takeaway or canteen-style plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white square/rectangular disposable paper plate, roughly 22 cm across. Area ≈ 22 x 22 x ~0.8 (rounded corners) ≈ 380 cm^2. Treating it as a round-equivalent ~22 cm plate: 3.14 x 11^2 ≈ 380 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Fried chicken pieces (bone-in, with batter/skin)
- Sliced cucumber
- Boiled cauliflower florets

STEP 4 - Area (share of plate):
- Chicken: ~35% (≈133 cm^2)
- Cucumber: ~20% (≈76 cm^2)
- Cauliflower: ~18% (≈68 cm^2)
- Total covered ≈ 73%, consistent with the visible food occupying most of the plate but not all of it.

STEP 5 - Volume (area x typical height):
- Chicken: 133 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 333 ml
- Cucumber: 76 cm^2 x 1.0 cm ≈ 76 ml
- Cauliflower: 68 cm^2 x 2.0 cm ≈ 136 ml

STEP 6 - Grams (bulk density):
- Chicken (meat, dense with bone): 333 x 0.8 ≈ 270 g (bone reduces mass, so 0.8 used)
- Cucumber (cut vegetable): 76 x 0.6 ≈ 46 g
- Cauliflower (cooked, cut): 136 x 0.6 ≈ 82 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Fried chicken with skin/batter: ~250 kcal/100 g → 270 g ≈ 675 kcal. Bone-in and fatty skin make this an upper-middle estimate; I use ~220 kcal/100 g as plated → 594 kcal.
- Cucumber: ~15 kcal/100 g → 46 g ≈ 7 kcal
- Cauliflower, boiled: ~25 kcal/100 g → 82 g ≈ 21 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 400 g of food, ≈ 620 kcal. For a visibly substantial fried chicken portion with vegetables on a ~22 cm plate, this is plausible. The chicken estimate is the largest uncertainty (bone and skin).

Totals: ~400 g, ~620 kcal.
